title: OAuth 2.0 is a framework for a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service
summary: OAuth 2.0 is a framework for a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service.
body: RFC 6749 says the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework enables a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service, either on behalf of a resource owner or on its own behalf. The source says: "arty application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service, either on behalf of a resource owner by orchestrating an approval interaction between the resource owner and the HTTP service, or by allowing the third-party application to obtain access on its own behalf." The access is limited and delegated. The framework is not a password-sharing protocol, and it is not an identity card by itself. What 'limited' means is the scope the authorization grants.
